title: Who approves what
summary: Choose who approves each kind of request, or that no approval is needed, by who asks and how much. Approvers decide from My decisions.

changes.text: Access control → Approvals: for attendance after the window, staff leave, course results, publishing a timetable, refunds, fines, fee waivers, scholarships, write-offs and more, choose no approval, or approval by a role, one person, the head of the department or the course's teacher. Rules can depend on who asks and on the amount; Try it shows who would decide.
My decisions: whoever is named as an approver sees the requests waiting for them at the top of their portal, with Approve and Reject.
Nothing changes until a rule is added. Nobody approves their own request, an Administrator can always decide, and rules about money wait for a second administrator.

title: Access control: who can do what
summary: Change what each role can do, make your own roles, and give or take single rights for one person, with safety checks and undo.

changes.text: Access control (System menu): for each role choose None, View or Edit per module, plus Approve; single rights under Advanced. See exactly what changes before saving.
Your own roles (e.g. Exam cell assistant), given to staff on the People tab or Employees → Extra access.
One person's own rights: give or take away single rights, until a date if you like. A right taken away wins over every role.
Money and control rights, and the Administrator role, wait for a second administrator to confirm. Every change is kept in History and can be undone.
Someone given pages of the administration sees Administration (given to you) in their portal switcher, with only those pages.

title: Ready for another institute
summary: A new institute sees only its own name everywhere, starts with a short first-run wizard, and can be shown a demo site with sample data first.

changes.text: First-run wizard for a brand-new institute: its name and contact details, logo and colour, and kind (university, affiliated college or school), then Set up your LMS.
The institute's own name everywhere: two-factor codes, calendar feeds, asset tags, emails and messages no longer mention any other institute.
Demo sites: sites.sh add-demo makes a separate site filled with sample data, with a Demo ribbon on every page and no backups.

title: Tours on every page, a To do bar, and Set up your LMS
summary: Every page has a guided tour. Everyone sees what still needs them until it is done. Administrators get a step-by-step checklist to set up a new institute.

changes.text: Tour button on every page: a guided tour of what the page is for, its tabs and main buttons. It starts by itself the first time you open a page.
To do bar at the top of your pages: your profile still to complete, phone notifications, and for teachers, students and parents the important things waiting for them.
Complete your profile: a checklist on your profile page. After 7 days, an incomplete profile opens first after sign-in; the menu still works.
Set up your LMS on the dashboard: the steps to start a new institute in order, each ticked when done, with Do it and Show me how.

title: Audit fixes: leavers' pay, students who leave, clearer messages
summary: Fixes from the November audit: leavers are paid for the days worked (not after resigning without 30 days' notice), and students who leave stop being charged hostel and transport. Several messages now say how to fix the problem.

changes.text: Someone who left during the month gets a payslip for the days they worked; before, they were left out of that month altogether. A resignation with less than 30 days' notice has that month's worked days withheld, and the payslip says why.
Leaving asks how they left (resigned with the day notice was given, terminated by the institute, or contract ended) and the last working day.
A student who leaves, is expelled or graduates: hostel stay, transport seat and mentor end that day, and the warden is told. Before, hostel rent and transport kept being charged every month.
A Dropped or Graduated student set by mistake can be put back to Active by an administrator within 30 days, with a reason.
Lifting a suspension lists the fees given to the student's class meanwhile, with one click to assign them.
Clinical rotation sheets show suspended students locked and leave out expelled ones. The exam-hall roll lists a suspended student as not allowed and leaves them out of the invigilator count.

Timetable clash messages name the class that is already there and show normal times (Monday 9:00 AM). Two people saving the same thing at once get a plain message instead of 'An unexpected error occurred'.
Each class in the Timetable's weekly view has links to change it from a date or to cover a class. Step 1 suggests grouping batch terms into a session when they are not grouped.

title: Hand over a teacher's work when they are away or leave
summary: When staff are suspended, on leave or leave the institute, their classes, courses, exam duties and roles are handed to others in one place.

changes.text: Employees → Hand over work. Away (suspended or on long leave): a cover for each class in the dates, or one teacher for all classes of a course. Leaving: a new teacher for each running course, and its timetable goes with it.
Hand over also gives back covers they were going to take, and moves their upcoming exam duties, school class-teacher roles and mentees. When they leave, committee seats and clinical supervision end.

Putting someone On leave, terminating them, or suspending or terminating them on a final warning now opens the hand-over. When they are back at work, covers still to come are taken back and the substitutes are told.
Committee member lists show a member who is away.

title: Visiting faculty paid per lecture
summary: Visiting faculty are paid for each lecture they take. The payslip shows every lecture not taken or covered by another teacher, with its date.

changes.text: Payroll → Visiting faculty: set a rate per lecture for each visiting teacher. A lecture counts when they mark its attendance. A lab double period counts as two lectures and a combined class as one; extra and make-up classes count too.

The payslip earns every lecture held, then deducts the ones not taken, covered by another teacher or marked by the office, with their dates. Days absent and late marks do not apply. A lecture sheet PDF lists every lecture.
The suggested pay for covering a visiting teacher's class is one of their lectures.
Visiting faculty see My lectures under My payslips: taken, not taken, covered, and the lecture sheet PDF.

title: One class for the same subject in several batches
summary: The same subject in two batch terms taught together (e.g. LB101 for BSN and AHS 1st) is easy to make one class: the clash message offers to combine, and the Timetable suggests it.

changes.text: Adding a class where the same subject of another batch already is no longer just says 'teacher busy' or 'room booked'. It names the other batch and offers Combine: one teacher, one room, one timetable, one exam paper, while each batch keeps its own students, attendance and results.

Timetable step 1 suggests subjects that may be taught together across the chosen batches, with a Combine button. Step 4 has a Taught together column with Combine and Separate. The draft notes same-teacher sections that are not combined.
The exam department can combine and separate sections from the Timetable.
The Courses list shows 'combined with' on each combined section, naming another batch's section with its term, e.g. 'A (AHS 1st)'.

title: Suspended and expelled students are locked
summary: A suspended student is locked out of attendance, exams, results and certificates until the suspension is lifted; an expelled student keeps only the leaving papers.

changes.text: A suspended student stays on the attendance sheet and marks sheet, greyed and marked Suspended. They cannot be marked, and those classes do not count for or against them.

Suspended students get no admit card and no seat in the exam hall. Their marks are locked and their result is held, so it does not hold up the rest of the class. The result is worked out when the suspension is lifted.

No certificates, result cards, library books, hostel or transport places for a suspended student. An expelled student gets only the migration and fee clearance certificates. Lifting the suspension removes every lock; past records are never changed.
The parent portal says when a child is suspended or no longer enrolled, and stays open to view records and fees.

title: Timetable wizard
summary: One step-by-step Timetable page with a guided tour, a safe way to clear a timetable and remake it, and the exam department can run it.

changes.text: Timetable and Smart timetable are now one page with six numbered steps, a ✓ / ! on each step, a readiness checklist, Back / Next and a guided tour. The batches you choose are carried into every step.

Timetable → Start again: clear the timetable of chosen batches from a date, to remake it from scratch. Each batch from its own start until its own end; classes before the date and classes with attendance are never touched. Preview first, then type CLEAR.
Timetable: make, clear and publish the weekly class timetable, with periods, rooms, teachers' free times and workload, the same as the administration.

title: Regulator returns
summary: Enrolment, teaching staff and results summaries for regulator returns.

changes.text: Reports → Regulator returns: enrolment, teaching staff and results summaries, on screen and as CSV.

title: Internship year
summary: Final-year interns: placements, duty hours verified by supervisors, leave, evaluations and completion.

changes.text: Clinical rotations → Internship: start internships, place interns, decide leave, mark complete; graduation lists check it.
Interns: verify logged duties and evaluate interns placed with you.
My clinical → Internship: log duties, ask for leave, follow your hours and evaluations.

title: Committees and minutes
summary: Committees with meetings, final minutes, decisions and action items that remind their owners.

changes.text: Committees: make committees with a chair, secretary and members; see every open action.
Committees: meetings, agenda, minutes and decisions (members only), minutes PDF, and your actions with daily reminders.

title: Student mentoring
summary: Every student gets a teacher as mentor, with private meeting notes and referrals to the principal.

changes.text: Mentors: give students a mentor (shared out evenly), and answer mentors' referrals.
My mentees: warning signs, follow-ups due, private meeting notes, refer to the principal.
Your home card shows who your mentor is (parents see it too).

title: Admissions moved out
summary: The Admissions screens are removed; admissions will have their own portal.

changes.text: Admissions (rounds, applicants, merit lists) is removed from this portal. New students are added under Students or by CSV import; students already admitted are not affected.

title: Graduation and alumni
summary: Graduation lists, degree and transcript tracking, and an alumni portal with a directory and surveys.

changes.text: Graduation lists: every student checked; graduate the cleared ones in one step; print the list.
Degrees & transcripts: track each one from request to hand-over.
An alumni login: degree and transcript status, your details, the alumni directory and surveys.

title: Exam paper files
summary: Teachers send question papers as PDF or Word files; the exam office prints them.

changes.text: Send exam papers: attach the question paper for each coming exam; see when it is printed or returned.
Exam paper files: who has sent their paper, download and print, mark printed or return with a note.

title: Hostel mess, roll call and transport
summary: Mess fees, the night roll call, transport routes, and monthly charges the accounts office approves.

changes.text: Night roll call (parents told about an absent resident) and a monthly mess fee per resident.
The month's hostel and mess charges are prepared as a draft; the accounts office approves them before they reach students' dues.
Transport: routes, stops with pick-up times, riders, and the monthly transport fee draft.
Monthly charges: approve or send back the hostel, mess and transport drafts.
The home card shows the transport route, stop and pick-up time.

title: Clinical rotations
summary: Hospital rotations for clinical groups, with clinical attendance, a signed logbook and placement letters.

changes.text: Clinical rotations: hospitals and wards, groups, supervisors (staff or a limited hospital login), the rotation schedule with clash checks, placement letters and group progress.
Clinical supervision: mark clinical attendance and sign logbook entries for the groups you supervise.
My clinical: your rotations, clinical attendance and logbook; add entries for your supervisor to sign.

title: Substitute teachers
summary: Classes of a teacher on leave get a free teacher proposed; the office confirms.

changes.text: Substitute teachers: approving leave proposes a free teacher for each class; confirm, change or cancel the class.
Substitute classes: the classes you cover, with attendance marking.

title: Home cards for families
summary: Parents see a card per child, students a Today card; phones are told about absences and results.

changes.text: Your children today: a card per child with today's attendance, fees to pay with Pay now, the next exam and the latest result.
A Today card on the home page: today's classes and attendance, Pay now, next exam, latest result.
Phone notifications when a child is marked absent in a class or a result is published (Settings → Rules → Reports can switch them off).

title: Outcome-based education (CLO/PLO)
summary: Course and program learning outcomes, mapped and measured from the marks, for accreditation.

changes.text: Outcomes (OBE): PLOs and pass levels per program, teachers' course files to lock or send back, and PLO attainment per program.
Course outcomes (OBE): CLOs with Bloom level mapped to PLOs, assessments tagged whole or by question part, part marks, and CLO attainment.

title: Exam seating and invigilation
summary: Seat students room by room, put invigilators in each room, and print door lists and attendance sheets.

changes.text: Seating & invigilation: rooms with rows × columns, seating that mixes papers in neighbouring columns, room grids, door lists and room attendance sheets.
Invigilators per room and time: proposed fairly (free teachers, never the paper's own teacher), editable, with a duty sheet and one message to each teacher.
Admit cards show the room and seat for each paper.
Exam duties list the papers seated in your room; you can mark their exam roll.

title: Semester rollover wizard
summary: End a session and start the next in four checked steps, with undo for promotions.

changes.text: Teaching & exams → Semester rollover: close the terms, promote students (hold back with a reason, carry-over subjects listed, undo within 7 days), start the next session with the same teachers, and copy fee structures as drafts.

title: Data checker
summary: Find missing or wrong records in one place, with a link to fix each.

changes.text: System → Data checker: students, staff, academics and fees checked for gaps and mistakes (missing CNIC or mobile numbers, duplicates, subjects without a teacher, students with no fee …), each with Fix….
Students and Employees open already searched when you follow a Fix… link.

title: Morning summary
summary: Administrators get one short summary at 8 AM, Monday to Saturday.

changes.text: Morning summary at 8 AM (Monday to Saturday) as a notification and email: money, attendance, work waiting and problems. Monday's covers the weekend.
Reports → Morning summary shows the same figures any time, with links to each page.

title: My shortcuts
summary: Star the pages you use most: they stay at the top of your menu on every device.

changes.text: Press ☆ beside a page's title to add it to My shortcuts at the top of the menu (up to 12); ★ removes it. Kept for you on every device.

title: An easier menu
summary: Search the menu, open and close its groups, see where work is waiting, and find pages grouped by job.

changes.text: Search the menu: type part of a page's name (or another word for it) and press Enter. On a computer, / or Ctrl+K jumps to the search.
Menu groups open and close; the group of the page you are on is always open and the rest stay as you left them.
Numbers beside Approvals, Profile changes, Certificate requests, Admissions and Result Approval show the work waiting; a closed group shows its total.
The menu is grouped by job: Students, Teaching & exams, Fees & accounts, HR & payroll, Store & assets, Reports, Communication, Other offices, System. Setup pages moved to Settings → More tools.
The accounts office, exam office, warden and gate menus have groups too, with your own things under Me.

title: Fee defaulter follow-up
summary: One page to follow up overdue fees: the list by batch or session, SMS reminders now, promises to pay, and admit-card exemptions.

changes.text: Fee defaulters: everyone overdue, by session, batch term, program, semester, days overdue and amount, with CSV.
Send SMS reminders now to the selected students and/or parents: preview first; at most one fee SMS per student a day.
Promise to pay: until the promised date no fee reminder goes and the admit card is not held for fees.
Allow one student's admit card despite overdue fees, with a reason and optionally a last day; kept on record when revoked.
Finance reports: the phone numbers in the defaulters table are under the Phone heading again.

title: University Reg No deadlines
summary: Set the last day for each batch's university Reg Nos; everyone is reminded before it and admit cards are held after it.

changes.text: University Reg Nos → Deadlines: set the last day for one batch term or every batch of a session (affiliated programs), and see how many students still have no Reg No.
Reminders: the administration and exam office once a week, then daily in the last 7 days; each student without a Reg No gets a notification and an SMS (Settings → Rules → SMS can switch the SMS off).
After the deadline a student's admit card is held until the Reg No is entered; exempt one student with a reason (and optionally a last day). Exemptions are kept on record.
The internal award list warns which students have no Reg No yet, with the batch's deadline.

title: Supplementary university results
summary: Affiliated programs: import the university's supplementary (re-sit) result; it counts from then on and the first attempt is kept.

changes.text: University result: choose 'a supplementary (re-sit) exam' to import re-sit results. Only for subjects failed in the university's result; the latest attempt counts for GPA, transcript (S) and promotion.
Every university result is kept: the first attempt and each supplementary, with how many times the university revised it.

title: Server health
summary: See the server's disk, memory and load and each site's status, certificate, version and backups, and get warned before a problem becomes an outage.

changes.text: System → Server health: disk, memory, load, uptime; the site, its database, version and deploy time, HTTPS certificate expiry, uploaded files size and last backup (the owner institute sees every institute).
A Server problem notification when the disk is over 85%, a certificate expires within 14 days, a site or database is down, memory or load stays high for 10 minutes, or the server stops reporting.

title: One datesheet for a whole session, and the session report
summary: A Mid or Final datesheet can cover every batch term of a session, and each session has a report of students, attendance, results and fees by batch.

changes.text: Datesheets: choose 'Whole session: Fall 2026' to put papers from every batch term of the session on one datesheet, published once with admit cards.
Sessions → Report: per batch term, sections, courses, students, attendance (average and below the minimum), results by stage and fees (charged, paid, owed, overdue); download as CSV.

title: Sessions: group every batch's term (Fall 2026) and start the next one
summary: When each batch has its own term, a session such as Fall 2026 groups them: term lists are grouped by session everywhere, and the next session can be started for every batch in one step.

changes.text: Courses → Academic terms → Sessions: suggested from the term names (and dates), batches guessed for terms without one; you check and save. Nothing recorded on a term changes.
Term dropdowns are grouped by session (current first, older ones folded), and term tick-lists have Tick all per session.

Start next session: for every batch, the next semester's term (e.g. BSN 6th Fall 2026 → BSN 7th Spring 2027), its sections from the curriculum, and the promoted students enrolled; preview first, then all in one step.
A new term whose name contains a session (e.g. BSN 2nd Fall 2026) joins that session by itself.

title: Teacher workload and what is free
summary: See who is over- or under-loaded, keep every teacher within 12–18 credit hours a week (or their own range), get suggestions for the least busy teacher, and find free rooms and teachers for any period.

changes.text: Smart timetable → Teacher workload: each teacher's credit hours a week while the chosen terms run (combined classes once), periods a week, and Over / OK / Under their range.
Settings → Teaching load: 12–18 credit hours a week by default; a teacher can have their own range. A section that takes a teacher above their most is refused unless you give a reason (activity log).
Choosing a teacher for a section lists suggested teachers first (taught it before, under-loaded, least busy) with their load before and after.
Propose teachers for every section without one, within everyone's most; assign the ticked ones in one go.
Smart timetable → What is free: free rooms and teachers for every period, and any class's free periods.

title: Smart timetable: a whole term's timetable in one go
summary: Administrators can generate a clash-free timetable for whole terms as a draft, adjust it, and publish it from a chosen date. Teachers can mark the times they cannot teach.

changes.text: Academics → Smart timetable: generate a draft for one or more terms. No clashes for students, teachers or rooms; teachers' unavailable times and limits respected; labs as double periods in a lab; combined classes together; classes spread over the week, same period each day, compact days.
Check the draft by class, teacher or room; move, add or take out classes (checked, and pinned so they stay when you generate again); a list of anything that could not be placed and why.
Publish from a date: earlier classes and all attendance stay as they are; all or nothing; optionally tells teachers, students and parents.
Per section: classes a week (default: credit hours), lab as a double period, home room. Per teacher: unavailable periods, classes a day and periods in a row, and 'fixed by the administration'.
My Timetable → My available times: mark the periods you cannot teach.

title: Backups page: see every backup and download a complete copy
summary: Administrators can see when the institute was last backed up, how much is kept on the backup account and whether the monthly restore test passed, start a backup, and download the whole database or all uploaded files.

changes.text: System → Backups: last backup, space used on the backup account, database and file sizes, the copies kept (14 nightly + 8 weekly), the monthly restore test and the full history.
Back up now: the server makes the same backup as the nightly one, within a minute.
Download the whole database (.dump, opens in pgAdmin) or all uploaded files (ZIP). Needs your password (and 2FA code); only you can download it, for 1 hour; other administrators are told; logged.
A notification when a backup fails, when none has finished for 26 hours, or when the restore test fails (once a day until fixed).
The dashboard warns about a missed backup after 26 hours instead of 36.

title: Affiliated programs: internal marks and the university's result
summary: Each program says who conducts its exams. For a program affiliated with a university, the institute keeps internal marks, prints the internal award list with Reg Nos, and imports the university's result.

changes.text: Exams conducted by (Grading tables & mark split → Programs): this institute, or the affiliating university for the mid, final and/or practical.
For an affiliated program the university's parts cannot be added, entered or put on the institute's datesheet; publishing shows internal marks only.
Internal award list (PDF / CSV) with Reg Nos and the internal total scaled to the mark split.
University result tab: import the university's result by Reg No (marks and/or grade, optional pass/fail), with a preview. Transcripts, GPA and promotion use it.
Internal award list (PDF) on the Grading page.
The exam office now sees every program on Grading tables & mark split.

title: University Reg No and student field rules
summary: Each student can have the affiliating university's registration number, and the institute chooses which student details are required when adding or importing students.

changes.text: University Reg No on the student record, the Add student form and the CSV import. It is unique, searchable, and printed on award lists, admit cards, result cards, the gazette and transcripts.
University Reg Nos page: fill in Reg Nos one by one or from a CSV, with a preview before saving.
Field rules (CSV Imports): choose which student details are required. The template and the Add student form follow them; first and last name are always required.
Your university Reg No is shown on your profile.
Your child's university Reg No is shown beside the roll number.

title: Breaks, day-specific periods and changing period times
summary: Periods can be breaks, zero periods or library periods and apply to some days only; a period's times can be changed after the timetable is built; times show on the 12-hour clock.

changes.text: Daily periods have a type: class period, zero period / assembly, break / prayer / lunch, or library / self-study. Breaks show on every timetable and PDF; no class can be put in them.
A period can apply to some days only, e.g. a shorter Friday.
Change… a period's times after the timetable is built: preview first, classes move from the date you choose, later periods shift with it, and classes already held stay as recorded.
Times are shown on the 12-hour clock (1:30 PM instead of 13:30).

title: Several batches side by side
summary: One term per batch (e.g. BS Dental 4th, BS Anesthesia 4th): shared subjects become one combined class across terms, free periods show in red, and free periods can be filled automatically.

changes.text: Combined classes: a subject can now be combined with the same subject in another batch's term that runs at the same time, so the shared teacher is no longer 'already booked'.
Timetable → Batches side by side: the timetables of several batch terms in one grid, with every free period in red and a count per batch.

Fill free periods: proposes the classes each batch is still missing in its free periods (teacher, students and room all free), shows the plan, and adds it only when you confirm. Existing classes are not moved.
A subject shared by two programs no longer makes one batch's term look like the other batch's students: the timetable no longer refuses a class because the other batch has a class at that time.

title: Self-assessments, force-delete exam types
summary: Marks of paper quizzes and class tests in a separate Self-assessments module, and administrators can force-delete an exam type in use.

changes.text: Self-assessments: record marks of quizzes, class tests and assignments done on paper (type them in or upload a CSV). Students and parents see them with the class average. They never count in exams or results.

Result types: an exam type that subjects use can now be force-deleted after a warning with counts and typing its name; a CSV backup of its marks downloads first. Published results stay unchanged; subjects waiting for approval go back to their teachers.
The manual's Exam department chapter has a step-by-step tutorial with a worked example (AUST table, BSN split, a practical fail, re-sit and promotion).

title: User manual
summary: A Help & manual page in every portal and the full manual as a PDF, updated with every version.

changes.text: Help & manual in the menu: your own chapter of the manual, with a search box, and a Download as PDF button.
Dashboard → User manual (PDF): the complete manual, every role's chapter included, with a What changed chapter built from these release notes. The manual is updated with every new version.

title: Re-sit the failed part, promotion list, result documents
summary: Supplementary re-sits only the failed part (or both papers), a class result and promotion list, and award lists, result cards and the gazette with the affiliating body.

changes.text: Supplementary: a student who failed only the practical re-sits only the practical paper; theory only, the final; both, two papers. The table's re-sit cap applies.

Results → Class results & promotion: pick program, semester (year) and term to see GPA (or total, % and division for annual programs), status (Promoted, on probation, Not promoted, Result pending) and position holders. Tick and Promote; a promotion can be undone.

Documents with the affiliating body: award list per subject (button in each result sheet), semester / year result cards (one page per student) and the result gazette (roll order, position holders, signature lines). The transcript now names the affiliating body too.

title: Grading tables for each university and board
summary: Each program can use its own grading table (KMU, AUST, Sarhad, Board ...), with a mark split, theory and practical passed separately, and a re-sit cap.

changes.text: Results → Grading tables & mark split: one fully editable table per affiliating body: letters, grade points (fixed or sliding inside a band), divisions, overall/theory/practical pass marks, the re-sit cap, promotion and degree GPA, Semester or Annual. Ready-made drafts (AUST, KMU, Sarhad, Board) arrive marked Draft to be checked first.
Each program picks its table and its mark split (Sessional / Mid / Final / Practical); a subject can have its own split. Teachers' quizzes and assignments are scaled into Sessional.
Final and Practical marks are entered by the exam office; teachers enter Sessional and Mid-term.
Theory and practical/clinical must each be passed; the result shows which part was failed. A re-sit is capped by the table's limit. Published results never change when a table is edited.

title: Move a payment to the right fee
summary: A payment recorded on the wrong fee can be moved to the right fee of the same student, with an administrator's approval.

changes.text: Fee → payment row → Move to another fee…: pick the fee it should have paid and say why. It goes to Approvals; nothing changes until an administrator approves.

Approving a move puts the money on the right fee as paid on the original day, makes the wrong fee owed again with a 7-day fine-free pause, and keeps the receipt number (the receipt now names the right fee). Recorded in the audit log and the money review.
Fee statements now show credit moved to or from another fee in the running balance.

title: Room list, teacher leave, card check
summary: Rooms with seats, approved leave blocks free slots, and the card check page knows a card whose term has not started.

changes.text: Timetable → Rooms: list classrooms, labs and halls with seats. Once rooms are listed, the timetable takes only listed rooms big enough for the class, and teachers booking make-up or extra classes are offered only rooms that fit. The room box on a course's timetable suggests listed rooms.
Free slots: days on approved leave show no free periods, and a booked class for a leave day cannot be approved.
Scanning a student card whose term has not started yet now says "Genuine, but not valid yet" with its dates.

title: Make-up and extra classes; cards for the batch term
summary: Teachers find free periods and book make-up or extra classes for approval. Student ID cards run for the student's batch term.

changes.text: My Timetable → Free slots & extra classes: pick your course to see the periods when you, its students and a room are all free. Book a make-up for a missed class (cancelled or attendance not taken) or an extra class for a course that is behind. The slot is held while an administrator decides.

Make-up and extra class requests arrive in Approvals. Approving checks the slot again, adds the class to the timetable and attendance, marks the missed class as made up and tells the students and the teacher.

Student ID cards are valid from the start to the end of the student's own batch term (Courses → Academic terms). If a student's batch term is not set up, the card runs the months in Settings and a warning names those students.

title: Each batch keeps its own term
summary: A term can belong to one batch (program + semester), and a fee for several batches shows every student their own batch term.

changes.text: Courses → Academic terms: give a term its batch (program and semester), e.g. "Fall 2026 BSN 8TH" = BSN, semester 8. Terms whose name already says so were filled in for you; check the new Batch column.

Fee structures: a fee for several batches can use "Each student's own term". Every student's fee, challan and receipt then shows the term of their own batch instead of one batch's term. A batch's own term can no longer be put on a fee that covers other programs or semesters.
Fee structures → Term…: correct the term on an existing fee. Amounts, instalments, payments and fines are not changed; it is recorded in the audit log.

title: Due dates for one program or semester; short attendance shown clearly
summary: Change a due date for one program, semester or section, and results no longer show short-attendance students as Failed during the term.

changes.text: Fee structures → Change due date: choose a program, semester and/or section to move the instalment only for those students (leave them blank for everyone on the fee). While you choose, it shows how many students it will move and any late fines built up, which you are asked to keep or remove before anything changes.

Results: a student below the minimum attendance is no longer shown as Failed while the term runs. The result sheet shows the grade their marks earn and "Short attendance": they are barred from the final exam (as on the exam roll and admit card). If still short when results are published, the subject is recorded as Short attendance and must be repeated.

title: The accounts office can move a due date
summary: The accounts office can now move one student's instalment due date (it used to get a missing permission error).

changes.text: Changing the due date of a student's instalment no longer says the permission is missing. If a late fine has built up you are warned first: keep it (added to Fines) or remove it, for example when the payment was marked late by mistake. Removing is kept on record with your reason and name. Moving a due date for everyone on a fee stays with the administrator.

title: The accounts office can remove a wrong late fine
summary: When a payment is recorded with an earlier date, the accounts office can now remove the late fine itself, with a reason kept on record.

changes.text: Recording a payment or a challan with an earlier date still shows the late fine it would take away. You can now choose either to keep it or to remove it yourself (for example when the payment was marked late by mistake); removing needs a reason, which is kept on record with your name. Moving a due date is unchanged.

title: Father's name in the accounts office; student lookup
summary: The accounts office now sees each student's father (or guardian) wherever it searches, lists or prints fees, can find a student by the father's name or CNIC, and has a read-only Student lookup.

changes.text: Wherever you search or pick a student (Student accounts, Fees list, Refunds, Previous dues, Fines), each student shows the father, e.g. 'Ali Khan s/o Ahmed Khan', so two students with the same name are easy to tell apart. When no father is on record, the main guardian is shown with the relation, e.g. 'Guardian: Sara Bibi (Mother)'.
You can now find a student by the father's name or the father's CNIC (with or without dashes); brothers and sisters come up together.
Fee challans, payment receipts, fee statements and the defaulters list (also its spreadsheet) show the father's name.
Student lookup in the accounts menu: find any student and open a read-only record with their details, father / guardian and fees, and a button straight to their fee account.

title: Late fines are protected; ID cards with a back side
summary: A late fine already built up no longer disappears without a warning, and ID cards have a validity you set and a printed back side.

changes.text: Moving a due date when a late fine has already built up now shows a warning with the amount. The fine so far is kept (added to Fines) and lateness counts again from the new date. Only an administrator can remove it instead, and that is kept on record.

Recording a payment or a challan with an earlier date that would take away a late fine now shows a warning. The fine is kept (added to Fines) and the payment keeps its real date. Only an administrator can remove the fine, with a reason kept on record.
Student ID cards are valid for the number of months set in Settings → Rules → Certificates (6 unless changed); staff cards for a year. Scanning an expired card shows that it has expired.

ID cards now have a back side: the logo, numbered instructions, where to return a found card, and the signature. It prints on the next page, placed for double-sided printing. Write your own instructions in Settings → Look & documents → Back of ID cards.

title: School mode: school fees
summary: For schools: monthly fee vouchers made on the 1st with tuition, transport and annual charges, sibling discounts, admission fees and a fixed late fine.

changes.text: Classes & sections has a Fees tab: set each class's monthly tuition, admission fee and annual charges for the session, add van and bus routes with their monthly fee, and put students on a route.

Each month your child gets one fee voucher on the 1st: tuition, transport (if on a route) and, on the first voucher of the session, the annual charges. It is due on the 10th (set in Settings). Pay it at the bank, by 1Bill or at the school, as before. You are told when it is ready.
Brothers and sisters (same guardian CNIC) get a sibling discount on tuition: 10% for the second child and 20% for the third and later (set in Settings). It is shown on the voucher.

A voucher paid after its due date has a fixed late fine, once (Rs. 200 unless changed in Settings), not a daily one. When you put a new student in a section, tick New admission to charge the class's admission fee.

title: School mode: exams, report cards and promotion
summary: For schools: 1st Term, Mid-Term and Final exams, marks entry by subject teachers, report cards for students and parents, and moving students up to the next class.

changes.text: Classes & sections has a new Exams & results tab: set up the 1st Term, Mid-Term and Final exams, set each subject's total marks (100 unless changed), follow how far marks entry has got in every class, and publish report cards class by class. Students and parents are told when a report card is ready.

Exam marks & report cards: subject teachers enter marks for their sections (tick Absent for a student who missed the paper; it counts as 0). The class teacher also writes remarks and rates skills and behaviour A to D.

Report cards show each subject's marks and grade, the total, position in the section (students with the same marks share a position), attendance, skills and remarks, and can be downloaded as a PDF. Grades follow the board scale; O and A Level classes use the Cambridge scale.

After the Final exam the report card shows the year's result, weighted 20% 1st Term, 30% Mid-Term and 50% Final (changeable in Settings). Promotion moves the students of a class to the next class in the new session: those who passed are ticked, others are kept back or promoted on approval, and Class 8 and 10 students can be placed in their chosen stream.

title: School mode: roll call, homework diary and parent-teacher meetings
summary: For schools: the class teacher's morning roll call with messages to parents, a homework diary, and parent-teacher meetings that parents book.

changes.text: My class: the class teacher marks the section Present, Late, Absent or Leave each morning. Parents of an absent or late child are told at once, in the parent portal and by SMS or WhatsApp. If the class teacher is away, the office can choose a teacher to cover that day.
For school classes the morning roll call is the attendance: each subject's attendance %, admit cards, warnings and the parents' notes use it, and teachers no longer mark attendance in every period.

Homework diary: subject teachers set homework for their sections, with a due date and an optional worksheet (PDF or picture). Students and parents see it at once, and each family gets one message with the day's homework in the evening (the time is in Settings).

Diary & attendance shows your child's homework and a month of attendance. Parent-teacher meetings: when the school sets a meeting day, book a time with the class teacher, and change or cancel it until the day.

Classes & sections now has Roll call (every section's roll call for a day: taken or not, absent and late, open it to correct, set a cover teacher) and Parent-teacher meetings (set a day and minutes per meeting, see bookings, cancel).
Right after changing a first-time password, the portal sometimes showed the change-password page again for a few seconds. It now opens straight away.

title: Combined classes
summary: One teacher can teach the same course to several programs together, e.g. AHS201 for BS Anesthesia and BS Dental, at the same time in the same room.

changes.text: Course section → Overview → Combined class: combine sections of the same course (e.g. section A for BS Anesthesia and section B for BS Dental). They get one teacher and one timetable, with no clash for sharing the teacher and the room. A section without a timetable gets the other's. Each section keeps its own students, attendance, marks and result sheet. A section can be taken out again.

A combined class shows as one class in Attendance and Grading: one list of all its students, each with their program. Attendance and marks are saved to each student's own section, and Submit sends every section's marks.
In a combined class, a timetable slot added, changed or removed in one section is done in all of them, and so is a change of teacher or of the marks scheme.
A combined class has one paper on the datesheet for all its sections: the exam roll, admit cards, clash checks and the number of teachers on duty count every section's students.

title: School mode: classes and sections
summary: A copy can now run a school: classes from Playgroup to Class 12 and O / A Levels, sections with class teachers, subjects and subject teachers.

changes.text: Settings → Institute type: choose School or College / University. A school gets Classes & sections, and the menus use school words (Subjects instead of Courses, Classes instead of Programs). Nothing changes until it is switched on.

Classes & sections → Set up classes: tick Pre-school, Class 1-5, Class 6-8, Matric (Science, Computer Science, Arts), Intermediate (Pre-Medical, Pre-Engineering, ICS, I.Com, F.A.), O Level or A Level, name the session (e.g. 2026-27) and the sections. Each class gets its usual subjects and knows the next class for promotion. Running it again only adds what is missing.

Each section: choose the class teacher, room and seats, and the teacher of every subject. Teachers are told about their new class. Add or remove subjects (optional "choice" subjects for O / A Levels), and add sections.

Put students in a section: they are enrolled in all the class's subjects (and the choice subjects you tick) in one step. A student can move to another section before classes start, taking their subjects along.

title: Exam duty and the exam roll
summary: Put teachers on exam duty with suggestions of who is free, and take a separate attendance in every paper.

changes.text: Datesheets → Duty on each paper: the system says how many teachers are needed (one for every 30 students, changeable in Settings → Exams & results) and lists the teachers who are free at that time first. A teacher with a class or another duty then is marked busy, with the reason. Choose the suggested teachers in one click and mark one as in charge. Duties can be changed until the paper starts.

Exam duties shows the papers you are on duty for. You are told when you are put on duty, taken off, or when the paper's date, time or room changes (also by SMS or WhatsApp when it is switched on in Settings).

Exam roll: on the exam day the teachers on duty mark each student present, late or absent. Only students allowed to sit the paper are listed; students held back by short attendance or unpaid fees are shown apart with the reason. It does not change anyone's class attendance. The exam office can correct it later.
Grading: a student marked absent in an exam paper shows as "Absent" in marks entry for that result type. When creating a datesheet, the exam office can say which result type its marks go into.
Unfair means cases: a teacher on duty can report cheating with a note. The exam office is told and records a decision. Cases are kept on record.
On phones, some wide tables shown as cards had their first line hidden behind a blank bar. Fixed.

title: Task map, notification tones and a message for every change
summary: See who gives tasks to whom on a map, hear a tone when a notification arrives, and get told whenever the office changes something about you.

changes.text: Tasks → Task map: a picture of who gives tasks to whom. Thicker arrows mean more tasks; colours show late, in progress, waiting, done or rejected. Click a person or an arrow to see the tasks. The admin sees everyone; staff see their own.

A notification tone plays in the portal when something new arrives (also in a background tab): the admin picks it for everyone in Settings → Notifications, including long ringtone-like tones and a separate alarm for urgent notices. Phones vibrate longer for urgent notices, and urgent alerts stay on screen until opened.

You are told when the office changes something about you: working hours, attendance corrections, salary, bonus, job role, status, password reset, record details; for students also courses and sections, marks, leave, hostel and fee changes; and everyone in a class when its timetable changes.
Dashboards show only the latest announcement, with View all for the rest.

title: Announcements from teachers and staff
summary: Teachers and staff can write announcements; the admin approves them before anyone sees them. The student home page now starts with the latest announcements.

changes.text: Post an announcement: teachers, heads of department, the principal and other staff write a notice for students (all, by program and semester, or a course section) or for colleagues. It is issued in their own name and job, and goes live once the admin approves it.
Announcements → Waiting for approval: approve and publish, edit first, or send it back with what to change. The writer is told either way and can fix it and send it again.
Home page order: the latest 3 announcements first (new ones marked), then the key numbers, then alerts and deadlines, then today.
Announcements can also be aimed at chosen semesters or course sections.

title: Warnings to students and staff
summary: The admin can give formal warnings with a violation from a list. The 3rd warning within 12 months is final, and the admin or principal decides the action.

changes.text: Warnings: find a student or staff member, choose the violation from the list, write what happened. Each warning counts for 12 months; the 3rd is final. The list of violations can be edited, and a warning given by mistake can be withdrawn with a reason (it stays on record).

Final warnings wait for a decision by the admin or principal: final chance, suspension (cannot sign in until it is ended), expulsion or termination, or a fine. The decision is applied to the person's record.
My warnings: read each warning, confirm 'I have read this', and reply once with your side.
Settings → SMS messages: a switch to also tell a student's guardian about a warning (off unless switched on).

title: WhatsApp messages, with documents
summary: Messages to students and parents can now go by WhatsApp, with the challan, receipt, result card or certificate attached. SMS is used only when WhatsApp fails.

changes.text: Messages from the institute arrive on WhatsApp, with the PDF attached: the challan with a fee reminder, the receipt when a payment is received, the result card with results, and the certificate when it is ready.
A message when a fee payment is received, with the receipt number.
SMS & WhatsApp page: set up WhatsApp (Meta's official WhatsApp Cloud API, or any provider's web link) and send a test. Each message shows whether it went by WhatsApp or SMS.
Settings: two new message switches (payment received, certificate ready).

title: Certificates on request and a monthly report
summary: Students ask for certificates from their portal and download them once approved and paid. The principal gets a monthly report on the 1st.

changes.text: Certificates: ask for a bonafide, character, completion, provisional (result), migration / NOC certificate or a fee clearance letter. Once the office approves it and the fee is paid, download it from the portal. Anyone can check it with the QR code.
Certificate requests: approve (with the fee from Settings, or change or waive it) or refuse with a reason. Anything still outstanding is shown before approving.

Monthly report: fees received and still owed, class attendance by teacher and class, results and pass rates, and staff attendance and leave. A message on the 1st of every month, with a PDF to download; any month can be opened at any time.
Settings has a new Certificates section with the fee for each certificate.

title: A "Today" view for students
summary: The student home page now opens with what matters today: classes, what is due this week and the latest marks.

changes.text: Today: the day's classes (the one running now is highlighted), everything due in the next 7 days (assignments, fee instalments with the consumer number, exams) and the latest marks.
On a phone the number tiles are smaller and the class list shorter, so the day's information fits on the first screen.
Results now has its own button in the phone's bottom bar.
Bigger buttons on touch screens, and the language button no longer gets cut off.

title: اردو — Urdu for parents and students, and fee reminders
summary: Parents and students can use the portal in Urdu, get a reminder before a fee is due, and parents hear on Monday if their child needs attention.

changes.text: Urdu: tap "اردو" on the sign-in page or at the top of any page. The choice is kept on the account and also used for SMS.
Fee reminders 7 days and 3 days before a challan is due, and on the due date, with the amount and consumer number. Only while it is unpaid.
Monday note to parents when a child needs attention: attendance below 75%, low marks so far, or missed assignments. Sent only when something changed.
The parent home page now also lists low marks and missed assignments.
Settings → SMS: switches for the fee reminder and the Monday note to parents.

title: A full portal for parents
summary: Parents now have their own pages for fees, marks, timetable and notices, for each of their children.

changes.text: Fees: what is due, with the challan to download and the consumer number for paying online, and every payment with its receipt.
Marks: quiz, assignment and exam marks in each subject as the teachers enter them, with the total so far.
Timetable & exams: classes for the next two weeks and the exam datesheet with the admit card.
Notices: the institute's announcements for the child's class.
Students now also see each mark as soon as the teacher enters it. The final grade still appears when results are published.
Parents with more than one child switch between them with one tap, and the portal remembers the last one chosen.

title: Fix: link previews on WhatsApp
summary: Shared links to the portal now show the picture card on WhatsApp and other apps.

changes.text: When the portal's link or the "what's new" link was shared on WhatsApp, the preview picture did not appear. It now does.

title: Pay fees online with 1Bill (ready for the bank)
summary: Everything is ready for students and parents to pay fees from any bank app, JazzCash or Easypaisa. It starts working as soon as the bank switches it on.

changes.text: Pay a fee challan through 1Bill from any bank app, JazzCash, Easypaisa, an ATM or a bank counter, using the consumer number on the challan. A late fee, if any, is included, so one payment settles everything.
The receipt appears straight away, with a message in the app and by SMS.
1Bill payments: every online payment of the day, with totals per bank, to match with the bank's statement.
Settings → Fees → Online payment: choose a charge added to each online payment to cover the bank's fee.
Share button next to the version: send the link on WhatsApp or anywhere else. Links to the portal and to "what's new" now show a preview picture with the institute's name.

title: Students to watch, and course feedback from students
summary: Teachers see early which students may need help, and students can say anonymously how each course went.

changes.text: Students to watch: a list of students in your courses whose attendance is below 75%, who have less than half of the marks given so far, who missed 2 or more assignments, or whose fee is overdue for 30 days or more. Each shows why, so you know what to talk about.
Your home page tells you how many students need attention, with a link to the list.

Course feedback: in the last two weeks of each term, students rate each course and teacher from 1 to 5 and can add a comment. It takes about two minutes and is anonymous: answers are saved without names.
Student feedback: see the averages and comments for your courses once their results are published, when at least 3 students answered.
Course feedback overview for the principal, HOD and admin: response rates while the survey is open, and scores for every teacher and course after the term. Admins can change the questions.
Students get a reminder in the app when the survey opens and two days before it closes.
The version number now sits right under the logo in the menu, so it is easy to find, and new versions are celebrated with a little confetti.

title: Version number, What's new, and faster photos
summary: You can now see which version of the system you are using and what changed in each update. Photos load faster.

changes.text: The version number is shown in the menu of every staff portal. Click it to see what's new.
After each update, a short "A new version is here!" message appears once.
A status page shows whether everything is working and which version you are using.
Photos you upload now load faster and take less space, and still look sharp. PDFs and Word or Excel files stay exactly as uploaded.
The system now tidies up after each update, so it keeps running smoothly over time.
Fixed a false warning that made parts of the system look like they had a problem when they were working fine.
Stronger protection for the institute's records, with copies kept safely in a second place every night.

title: Fix: removing a course offering
summary: Deleting a course offering by unenrolling its students works again.

changes.text: Deleting an offering and unenrolling its students showed "An unexpected error occurred", even when no attendance or marks had been entered. It now works. Offerings that already have attendance or marks are still protected and cannot be deleted.

title: Two-step sign-in for administrators, daily money review
summary: Administrator accounts are now protected by a code from a phone app, and every change to money is listed for a daily check.

changes.text: Administrators sign in with their password plus a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator). A trusted device is remembered for 30 days.
If an administrator loses their phone, another administrator can reset their two-step sign-in from Activity → Security.
Activity → Money changes lists every discount, refund, cancelled receipt and fee change, so they can be checked day by day and marked as checked.
A reminder appears at 8 AM when there are money changes from earlier days that nobody has checked yet.
Links in notifications now open the right tab of a page (for example the leave or fines tab).

title: Attendance fine warnings for students and parents
summary: Students and parents can see early whether low attendance will lead to a fine, and how many classes are needed to avoid it.

changes.text: For each subject, students and parents see the attendance band they are in, the fine it would bring, and how many more classes are needed to get back to a safe level.
The admin dashboard shows how many leave requests are waiting and how many students are at risk of an attendance fine.
Sick leave requests need a medical note attached.
The Apply button for leave no longer stays greyed out after a missing-note message.

title: Attendance fines, course rules, staff leave and timetables
summary: A large update: attendance fines by band, rules for which courses a student may take, staff leave requests, printable timetables, safer discounts and a safe nightly copy of all records.

changes.text: Attendance fines per subject by band: 75% and above no fine; 65–74% Rs 3,000; 55–64% Rs 6,000; 45–54% Rs 10,000; below 45% is sent to an administrator to decide. Fines are charged before final exams.
Every Monday, an app message (and SMS if switched on) warns students whose attendance in a subject is in a fine band, with the fine it would mean.
Courses can require earlier courses to be passed first. An administrator can allow an exception.
Each programme has a limit on credit hours per semester (for example 21). An administrator can allow a student to take more.
Staff apply for leave in the app; an administrator approves it and payroll takes it into account. Sick leave is paid up to the yearly allowance set in Settings → Payroll.
Timetables can be printed per class, for the whole institute and per teacher.
Discounts now apply to tuition fee only by default, so other charges (like the student card) are no longer discounted by mistake.
Every night, a safe copy of the institute's records is kept in a second place.

title: Starting point
summary: The system as it was before release notes were kept: admissions, students, staff, courses and results, attendance, fees and receipts, payroll, library, hostel, gate, announcements and the student and parent portals.

changes.text: Email address verification, copies of important emails to administrators, and a friendly "Page not found" page.
